Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates unilateral hyperlucency of the right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings and a smaller right hilum, which are classic features of Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome (post-infectious obliterative bronchiolitis). This condition explains the patient's history of recurrent lung infections and is consistent with the imaging findings, unlike pneumothorax or technical error.
